references.text: God gives Abraham a similar blessing to become a great nation and to give land to his descendants
God renews the promise to Abraham to make him a multitude of nations and to give the land of Canaan to his descendants as an everlasting possession
God repeats the promise to Isaac to give these lands to his descendants and to make his descendants as numerous as the stars
Isaac blesses Jacob with the blessing of El Shaddai to make him fruitful and numerous into a community of nations, and to give him Abraham's blessing with the land as an inheritance
God repeats the promise to Jacob at Bethel about a nation and a community of nations that will come from him, and the land that will be given to his descendants
God promises Jacob in a vision that He will make him into a great nation
A direct theological connection where Jacob confirms that he has received the same promise of 'nations' that was given to Abraham.
Connects the promise to Isaac with the confirmation to Jacob, showing the continuity of God's promise of land and numerous descendants.
Jacob quoted in 48:4 the same promise of 'nations' and kings that God gave him personally in 35:11.
Ezekiel confirms that the promise of an 'everlasting possession' given to the fathers (as Jacob mentions) still stands as an oath.
Jacob confirms in 48:4 that he has received the same promise to become the father of a 'multitude of nations' as was given to Abraham.
